independent_deductions: The tangent at a differentiable point xk is y=f(xk)+fprime(xk)(x-xk). If fprime(xk) is nonzero, solving its zero gives xnext=xk-f(xk)/fprime(xk). This is an exact tangent intercept, not necessarily a root of f. Each iterate must remain in the domain, and no universal convergence follows. For x²-3 the source p3 denominator 2x in the first substitution must be 2x0.

For the positive square-root example, xnext=(x+3/x)/2 and the five exact iterates from x0=1 are 1,2,7/4,97/56,18817/10864. The original table mislabels iterate values as y even though y earlier meant f(x); its absolute errors are coarse bounds rather than equalities. Decimal corroborations are separately recorded below. Figures 1-3 are schematic tangent constructions; their intercept ordering is coherent.

With r=sqrt(3), xnext-r=(x-r)²/(2x). For any x0>0, x1>=r; thereafter xnext<=x since x>=r, while xnext>=r. Thus a positive nonincreasing bounded tail converges to a nonzero limit. Passing to the limit in the recurrence then yields +sqrt(3), with no prior unjustified assumption of convergence. The error identity gives local quadratic convergence. Negative starting values stay negative and the same magnitude recurrence yields -sqrt(3); x0=0 is undefined. Digit doubling is a local rate description, not a promise for every function/start.

The source Figure 5 and accompanying warning depict a two-cycle, despite its caption incorrectly claiming convergence to an unexpected root. A direct mathematical witness is f(x)=(5x-x³)/2: f(-1)=-2, f(1)=2 and fprime(±1)=1, hence Newton maps -1 to 1 and 1 to -1 forever. The negative-root convergence of Figure 4 and this nonconvergence are different outcomes.

For a ring at (x,y) below two fixed supports (0,0),(a,b), let r1=sqrt(x²+y²),r2=sqrt((a-x)²+(b-y)²). The source Figure 6 right-distance label incorrectly has (b-y²) rather than (b-y)², while its constraint r1+r2=L is correct. The position sought is the ring, not the string. A taut inextensible negligible-mass string and frictionless freely sliding ring under uniform gravity support the stated model. A nondegenerate ellipse requires L>sqrt(a²+b²); otherwise the feasible set is empty (strictly smaller L) or the support-joining segment (equality).

At a smooth local lower-branch stationary point, differentiating r1+r2=L gives (x+yyprime)/r1+(x-a+(y-b)yprime)/r2=0. Setting yprime=0 yields x/r1=(a-x)/r2. For the depicted a>0 and point below both supports, both angles to the upward vertical are acute, so equality of their sines entails equal angles. Equal horizontal tension components cancel; with common tension T, the upward components balance the ring weight via 2T cos(alpha). The vertical line is the normal to the ellipse at its lowest point, matching the stated reflection-angle interpretation there.

Write s=sqrt(L²-a²)>|b|. Then ystar=(b-s)/2 and xstar=a(s-b)/(2s). Direct substitution gives r1=L(s-b)/(2s),r2=L(s+b)/(2s), positive lengths whose sum is L and with equal horizontal ratios a/L. The lower point has ystar<min(0,b) and, for a>0,0<xstar<a. The implicit derivative denominators are nonzero there; Fy=ystar/r1+(ystar-b)/r2<0 establishes the local branch condition. The full ellipse is not one global function y(x).

A global minimum requires more than the stationary condition. Triangle inequality for vectors (x,-y) and (a-x,b-y) gives L=r1+r2>=sqrt(a²+(b-2y)²). Therefore |b-2y|<=s and y>=(b-s)/2. The candidate above attains the bound, proving global minimality. Equality in the vector inequality fixes the candidate (also at a=0, where the drawing collapses but the coordinates remain well-defined for L>|b|). For L=sqrt(a²+b²), minimum y on the support segment is min(0,b); the formula is not to be used if s=0.

All substantive checks use the supplied source, direct geometry and elementary algebra/calculus; no current external fact is asserted. The optical interpretation is scoped to the stated equal-angle model rather than an unprovided optical calculation.
